sections.name: SlideLayout
sections.title: Slide layout record
sections.what: Defines a simple record that holds one slide's width, height and a list of its shapes with their position and formatting.
sections.why: Gives the analyzer one consistent container for what it learns about a slide.
sections.watch_out: Sizes are stored in EMU units, a very fine PowerPoint measurement, so the numbers look large and are not inches.

sections.name: ApproachSlideTemplate
sections.title: Approach slide template record
sections.what: Defines the record that describes one approach slide: its kind, layout, title style, body style and any chart or table style.
sections.why: Gives every approach slide template the same fields so the generator can read them the same way.
sections.watch_out: The slide kind is a plain text label, so a misspelled label would quietly create a new category.

sections.name: ApproachSectionAnalyzer (part 1)
sections.title: Analyzer setup and start of analysis
sections.what: Creates the analyzer for a proposals folder, stores the RAG engine if one is given, and prints which detection method is in use. It then starts the main analysis, which lists the .pptx files and prepares empty collections for results. Without a RAG engine it uses a fixed list of approach words such as timeline, governance and week.
sections.why: Likely reason: keyword matching is a backup for when semantic search is not available.
sections.watch_out: Without the RAG engine detection is less accurate, and the console message warns about this.

sections.name: ApproachSectionAnalyzer (part 2)
sections.title: Loop over proposal files
sections.what: Goes through each proposal file, analyzes it, adds its results to the combined collections, and prints how many approach slides it found. A file that fails is reported and skipped so the run continues. The closing lines were cut off in the packet, so the final summary step is not described here.
sections.why: Likely reason: one unreadable file should not stop the whole analysis.
sections.watch_out: Failures are printed only when verbose is on, so a broken file can disappear without a trace.

summary: Reads the Approach slides of existing proposal PowerPoint files and works out a reusable layout and formatting pattern for each kind of approach slide. Only part of this file was visible in the packet, so later behavior is unconfirmed.
purpose: Give the proposal generator a pattern for timeline, governance, module and workstream slides so new proposals match the style of past ones.
why: Likely reason: so generated approach slides copy the look of real past slides rather than being drawn from scratch. The module docstring states this goal.
how: Open each proposal file, find its approach slides (by semantic search when a RAG engine is given, otherwise by a fixed keyword list), describe each slide's shapes, text and table formatting, then combine the results into one master template. Reason for the final combining steps not stated in the visible code.
inputs: A folder of .pptx proposal files (default data/proposals, a relative path), an optional RAG engine, and a verbose flag that controls printed progress.
outputs: A dictionary of slide templates grouped by type (timeline, governance, modules, workstreams), plus slide sizes, fonts, colors and layout patterns. The fallback case returns a default template.
risks: When verbose is off, a proposal that fails to analyze is skipped with no message. The default folder path depends on where the program is started. Most methods were not visible in the packet.
debug: Turn on verbose and look for lines starting with a warning about a file name. Check that the proposals folder resolves from the launch directory. If templates come back empty, check the keyword list and whether the slides contain those words.
